pl-l3d34c3-d1e115.summary: Shows from Isaiah that the same gifts were in Christ: a shoot from the root of Jesse, on whom the spirit of the Lord rests, the spirit of wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, and fear of the Lord.
claims: The seven gifts were in Christ.

pl-l3d34c3-d1e121.summary: Objects with Bede on Proverbs that all fear will cease: there are two fears, servile, the beginning of wisdom, which perfect charity casts out, and friendly, which accompanies perfect wisdom, a holy fear lasting forever, by which a son fears to offend the father; yet both will cease in the future, while charity never fails.
claims: Bede says both servile and friendly fear will cease in the future.

pl-l3d34c3-d1e144.summary: Adds Augustine on the Psalm: fear of the Lord is a great help for those advancing to salvation, but is cast out for those who arrive, for they no longer fear a friend once they reach what was promised.
claims: Augustine says fear is cast out from those who arrive at the promise.

pl-l3d34c3-d1e157.summary: Draws out that these authorities signify there will be no fear in the future.

pl-l3d34c3-d1e160.summary: Infers the difficulty: if fear will not be in the future, neither will the seven gifts, nor are they now in angels or holy souls.

pl-l3d34c3-d1e163.summary: Resolves the apparent conflict: the seven gifts are now in angels and blessed souls and will be in us in the future, but not all with their present uses. Filial fear now makes us fear to offend and be separated from the one we love, and to revere him; in the future it will make us revere him without fearing separation or offense. So fear of separation is not in angels or saints, but reverence, love mixed with subjection, which was also in Christ, 'heard for his reverence'.
claims: The gifts remain in the homeland with different uses.
Filial fear in the homeland is reverence without fear of separation.
Reverence is love mixed with subjection.

pl-l3d34c3-d1e172.summary: Reports that some contend fear is in Christ and the angels only by effect.
claims: Some hold that fear is in Christ and the angels only by its effect.

pl-l3d34c3.summary: Shows from Isaiah 11 that the gifts were in Christ. Bede and Augustine seem opposed, saying all fear will cease in the future, which would mean the seven gifts will not exist then and are not now in angels or saints. Lombard reconciles them: the gifts are in angels and saints and will be in us, but not with all their present uses. Filial fear now makes us fear to offend and be separated from the one we love, and also revere him; in the future it will make us only revere, without fear of separation. That reverence, love mixed with subjection, was also in Christ. Some hold that fear is in Christ and the angels only by its effect.
claims: The seven gifts were in Christ.
The gifts will remain in the future, but with changed uses.
In the homeland filial fear becomes reverence without fear of separation.
Reverence is love mixed with subjection, and was in Christ.
